outgoing.name: Athens
outgoing.excerpt: Athens and other Greek cities revolted in 88 BC, and the peninsula was crushed by the Roman general Sulla.

outgoing.name: Christianity
outgoing.excerpt: At the same time Greece and much of the rest of the Roman east came under the influence of Christianity.

outgoing.name: Homer
outgoing.excerpt: The epics of Homer inspired the Aeneid of Virgil, and authors such as Seneca the younger wrote using Greek styles.

outgoing.name: Olympic Games
outgoing.excerpt: The emperor Nero visited Greece in 66, and performed at the Olympic Games, despite the rules against non-Greek participation.

outgoing.name: Paul of Tarsus
outgoing.excerpt: The apostle Paul had preached in Corinth and Athens, and Greece soon became one of the most highly Christianized areas of the empire.
